    The Science Behind It

    Many people with nerve discomfort are also low in B12, the nutrient nerves need to build and maintain their protective coating. When that breaks down, signals misfire: tingling, burning, numbness. Most people have never had their B12 actually tested.

     

    Vitarosa delivers active B12 sublingually, absorbed directly under the tongue instead of through digestion. In a study of over 4,000 patients, this method outperformed B12 injections at raising serum B12.

     

    Once B12 is restored, nerves can rebuild what the deficiency broke down and start firing clean signals again.

    Is It Safe?

    Yes — our B-Complex supplement is 100% natural, non-GMO, vegan, and made without any artificial fillers or preservatives. All ingredients are third-party tested for purity and potency in a GMP-certified facility.

     

    B vitamins are generally well-tolerated. However, if you’re pregnant, nursing, or taking medication (especially blood thinners), we recommend consulting your healthcare provider before use — just to be safe.

    Ingredients

    Each serving (2 droppers) contains:

     

    – 5,000mcg Vitamin B12 (as Methylcobalamin) The active form your nerve cells use directly, no conversion required
    – 2,400mcg Vitamin B1 (as Benfotiamine) A well-absorbed form that supports healthy B1 levels, which diabetics lose far faster than non-diabetics
    – 400mcg Vitamin B9 (as Methylfolate) Bypasses the conversion step many people's bodies struggle with
    – 16mg Vitamin B3 (as Niacinamide) Supports nerve and cellular energy metabolism

     

    Deliberately excludes B6. Most B-complex formulas add pyridoxine by default. Regulatory agencies in Australia, Singapore, and New Zealand have warned that B6 can itself cause peripheral neuropathy at chronic doses, the exact symptom this product is meant to help with. We left it out on purpose.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    What makes Vitarosa different?
    Most B-complex supplements use cheap synthetic forms your body has to convert before it can use them, and most include B6, which can worsen nerve issues at chronic doses. Vitarosa uses active, bioavailable forms, methylcobalamin, methylfolate, and benfotiamine, delivered sublingually so they skip digestion entirely.

     

    Does this really help with nerve pain and neuropathy symptoms?
    Vitarosa restores B12 levels that metformin and other factors deplete, so nerves have what they need to maintain and repair their protective coating. Many people find that as B12 is restored, sensation and comfort improve. Individual results vary, and this product isn't intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

     

    Why sublingual instead of a capsule?
    A capsule has to survive stomach acid and gut absorption before any of it reaches your blood. Sublingual delivery skips that step. In a study of over 4,000 patients, it outperformed B12 injections at raising serum B12, without a needle or a clinic visit.

     

    How long until I notice a difference?
    This varies by person and by how depleted your B12 levels are to start. Consistent daily use matters more than any single dose.

     

    What's the correct dosage and how should I take it?
    Two droppers under the tongue, twice daily, morning and evening. Hold for 30 seconds before swallowing for best absorption.

     

    Are there any side effects?
    Vitarosa is well tolerated by most people. As with any supplement, individual sensitivities vary. If you notice anything unusual, stop use and consult your doctor.

     

    Is it safe to take with metformin or other diabetes medications?
    Yes, Vitarosa is designed specifically for people on metformin, since metformin is a primary driver of B12 depletion. If you have questions about your specific medications or health history, talk to your doctor. It's also worth asking whether your B12 has ever actually been tested. Most people on metformin have never had it checked.

     

    How is this better than a standard B12 supplement?
    Most standard B12 supplements use cyanocobalamin, a synthetic form your body has to convert before use, in capsule form that has to survive digestion. Vitarosa uses methylcobalamin, the active form nerve cells use directly, delivered sublingually so it never has to survive your gut.

    What Sets Our B-Complex Apart?

    Most B-complex supplements sound the same, but there are real differences that affect how well they actually work.

    Active, Bioavailable Forms

    We don't just add B12 for the label. We use methylcobalamin, the active form your nerve cells use directly, with no conversion step required. Most cheap B-complex formulas use cyanocobalamin, a synthetic form your body has to process first.

    Sublingual Delivery

    B12 is notoriously hard to absorb through digestion alone, especially for anyone whose gut is already working overtime. That's why Vitarosa is delivered sublingually, absorbed directly under the tongue. In a study of over 4,000 patients, this method outperformed B12 injections at raising serum B12.

    No B6, No Fillers

    Most B-complex formulas add pyridoxine (B6) by default. Regulatory agencies in Australia, Singapore, and New Zealand have warned it can itself cause peripheral neuropathy at chronic doses, the exact issue this product is meant to help with. We left it out on purpose, and we didn't pad the formula with anything else that doesn't earn its place.

    Have Questions? We Have Answers.

    I've had numbness for years. Can this actually still help me, or is it too late?

    Nerve damage that's gone on for a long time is harder to reverse than newer damage, but many people still see B12 status affecting their symptoms even after years of neuropathy. There's no way to promise a specific outcome for your situation, but restoring depleted B12 gives your nerves what they need to repair, whatever stage you're starting from.

    Will this replace my gabapentin or Lyrica?

    No, and you shouldn't stop any prescribed medication without talking to your doctor. Vitarosa isn't a substitute for medications your doctor has prescribed. It addresses a different piece of the puzzle, restoring B12 status, which may work alongside what you're already doing.

    I already take a multivitamin. Isn't that enough?

    Most multivitamins include a small amount of B12 in a form (cyanocobalamin) your body has to convert before use, and often include B6, which we deliberately leave out. If you're on metformin, a general multivitamin usually isn't giving your nerves what they specifically need.

    Is this just another supplement that's not going to do anything?

    That skepticism is fair, a lot of supplements overpromise. Vitarosa isn't built around a vague "vitamins are good for you" claim. It's built around a specific, documented mechanism: metformin depletes B12, B12 is required for nerve repair, and this delivers it in a form and method your body can actually use.

    Can I take this if I'm not diabetic?

    Yes. B12 depletion and its effect on nerve health isn't exclusive to diabetics or metformin users. Anyone dealing with nerve discomfort related to low B12, B1, or B9 status can benefit from this formula.

    What's the correct dosage and how should I take it?

    Two droppers under the tongue, twice daily, morning and evening. Hold for 30 seconds before swallowing for best absorption.

    Is it safe to take with medications?

    Vitarosa is designed specifically for people on metformin, since metformin is a primary driver of B12 depletion. If you have questions about your specific medications or health history, talk to your doctor. It's also worth asking whether your B12 has ever actually been tested. Most people on metformin have never had it checked.

    Are there any side effects?

    Vitarosa is well tolerated by most people. As with any supplement, individual sensitivities vary. If you notice anything unusual, stop use and consult your doctor.
